<reason>B more convincingly resolved the conflict between creator access and intermediaries’ commercial interests. A established a serious chokepoint concern, but did not justify requiring unlimited reputation-driven losses or restricting the motion to dominant platforms. B supplied enforceable access protections while preserving a narrowly justified refusal. A’s closing misrepresented that standard as permitting exclusion whenever partners might object, rather than answering its evidentiary threshold. A’s sweeping claims about other industries and reputation-only deplatforming also weakened its grounding.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s pressure-question answer specified independent review empowered to restore access, proof of substantial losses, and consideration of less restrictive measures. This directly defeated A’s claim that allowing any reputational defense necessarily produces zero enforceable duties. B then effectively exposed why A’s “ban with paperwork” response ignored those substantive protections.</best_rebuttal>
